case_title: One scanner offline in a non-urgent wave
exception_description: Wave RA-7012 has 12 standard orders. One handheld scanner is offline, but the remaining station can absorb the work with only a short queue increase. AI recommends keeping the current pick sequence and letting the open station clear the batch.
layer1_visible: Wave RA-7012 has 12 standard orders. One handheld scanner is offline, but the remaining station can absorb the work with only a short queue increase. AI recommends keeping the current pick sequence and letting the open station clear the batch.
detail_expand: A spare scanner can be fetched from maintenance, but that retrieval takes time and pulls labor from a nearby replenishment task. No rush orders are included in this wave. The case is designed as a low-risk resource decision where intervention mostly adds friction instead of reducing meaningful downside for the batch.
ai_recommendation: AI recommends keeping the current sequence because the remaining station can clear the batch and fetching backup equipment adds more cost than value.

current_disruptions.description: Pick station or scanner may be offline; throughput partially constrained

traceability_text.trace_rationale_short: The visible capacity loss is manageable, so stability is cheaper than intervention.
traceability_text.trace_more: Audit log stores scanner status, ETA check, and queue decision.
traceability_text.recommended_check: Check maintenance ETA for the spare scanner.

feedback_text.feedback_ai_outcome: The open station cleared the wave on time, so the simple path kept total cost lowest.
feedback_text.feedback_alt1_outcome: The spare-equipment check did not change the plan, but it added waiting and coordination cost.
feedback_text.feedback_alt2_outcome: The rebalance finished safely, yet the manual reshuffle created unnecessary labor and scanning overhead.
